title: List what two threads can read when nothing is reordered

blocks.text: Your team reviews lock-free code by writing each suspicious interaction down as a tiny program: a few threads, each a list of reads and writes of shared variables. `LitmusModel` lists every combination of values those reads can end with. Before it models what hardware and compilers do, it needs the baseline: the results the threads can produce when nothing is reordered, which is what the Java memory model promises a program without data races.

`LitmusModel.State` already performs one operation at a time and keeps memory and registers. Finish `explore(state, results)` in `src/main/java/practice/LitmusModel.java`: from `state`, add the registers of every finished execution to `results`. About eight lines in total.
When you're done, a reviewer can ask whether two threads that each set their own flag and then check the other's can ever both find the other's flag unset, and get an answer they can trust.

cases.says: a thread that only reads ends with the starting value 0 in every register
a read in one thread and a write in another can end either way round
a thread reading two variables written by two other threads can end with any of the four combinations
when each thread writes its own slot and then reads the other's, both can see the other's write, because the threads' operations interleave rather than run thread after thread
when each thread writes its own slot and then reads the other's, no execution ends with both reads seeing 0, because each thread performs its own operations in program order

origin.section: A Thread Keeps Its Own Order; Another Thread May See Its Accesses Reordered

concepts: If each thread keeps its program order, two threads that each write their own flag and then read the other's can't both read the old value; any interleaving lets at least one see the other's write.
Intra-thread semantics lets the compiler and processor reorder accesses to different variables, because the thread itself can't tell; another thread can.
